name: Dusk Blue
lede: Dusk Blue is a deep, slightly greenish blue that our library finds under three other names within two units of distance.

sections.title: A crowded corner of blue
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 reads the swatch as a pale purplish blue, about 7.1 units from the block center, and it is also carried in Wikipedia's X11 list and the 2010 xkcd color survey [1]. Our library ties the name to Crayola's list through a Wikipedia citation, and to the "dusk" family of names generally [1].

The closest near-duplicates, each under 2.4 units away, are [[dusk-blue]], Munsell's YInMn Blue and USAFA Blue [1]. The next distinct named color is [[light-navy]], about 4.8 units off, with [[cyanine-blue]] and [[lapis-lazuli]] further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 86 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.36 percent, more common than 50 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 15 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.9 percent of that period's paintings, 3.6 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1400 painting by Master of Heiligenkreuz, 555 years before the name's 1955 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph (and the matching "field" object) invented a country claim ("over-represented in Norwegian painting") with no basis — ar.co is empty for this slug — and the earliest-match painting+painter ("Giovanni di Paolo's Adoration of the Magi, 1450") doesn't match the real first-seen record (a 1400 painting by Master of Heiligenkreuz). The presence count (51) and peak stat (1910s/1.3%/6x+) also didn't match the real data (86 as-photographed; 1900s/0.9%/3.6x). Rewrote the paragraph directly from data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug; removed every unsupported claim rather than inventing a replacement for it.
